One value, several views
A single number feeds two independent displays. Change it once and watch both respond.

Next: Threshold logic combines conditions.

Use the tabs to explore the other examples.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click a component first. HTML: use controls directly.

2. Select either display and open Inputs… to inspect its source; rename instances there too.
3. Export HTML to operate the same drawing offline. Explore the other tabs for more examples.

A threshold with an enable switch
The alarm is on only when Signal level is greater than 70 AND Enabled is on.

70 → OFF
71 → ON, when enabled
Disabled → always OFF
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click a component first. HTML: use controls directly.

1. Signal level starts at 70: the alarm is OFF. Raise it to 71 and the alarm turns ON.
2. Switch Enabled off: the alarm stays OFF at every signal level.
3. Open Inputs… on Above 70? to change B or the comparison; inspect Both conditions to see both sources.
SMART COMPONENTS  /  03 OF 15
Scale a decimal signal
Multiply by two, limit the result to 0–10, then map that range to a percentage.

2.5 × 2 = 5
5 is halfway through 0–10
Halfway through 0–100 = 50%
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click a component first. HTML: use controls directly.

1. Decimal input starts at 2.5 with step 0.1: ×2 gives 5, which maps to 50%.
2. Try −2: the limiter produces 0. Try 7.5: the limiter caps 15 at 10, so the gauge shows 100%.
3. Open Inputs… to inspect the factor, bounds, and mapping. Fractional values travel through every connection.

Countdown from nine
A repeating pulse drives a countdown, a digit display, and a completion indicator.
enable
pulse
count
Zero reached
Restore the starting count
The count stays at 0 until reset.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click a component first. HTML: use controls directly.

1. Turn Run on. The first pulse arrives after 1 second; the count steps from 9 to 0. Done turns on at zero.
2. Switch Run off, then press Reset to 9 to restore the starting count. Further pulses at zero leave it at zero.
3. Timing pauses while this tab or browser page is hidden; return to continue the countdown.

Send a pulse into the future
A transport delay preserves every pulse, then the counter records each arrival.
every transition
same pulse, later
immediate
Reached turns on at 3 arrivals.
Further pulses keep counting.
Reset clears the count, not the delay queue.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click a component first. HTML: use controls directly.

1. Press Send pulse. Each completed click sends a 100 ms true pulse.
2. Input now flashes immediately. After delay flashes 1.5 seconds later, and Delivered pulses increases once per arrival.
3. Try three quick clicks: all three arrive in order. The counter’s Reset button clears the count; queued pulses still arrive.
4. Timing pauses while this sketch or browser page is hidden; return to continue its pending pulses.

Routing · choose a channel
Four numeric inputs feed one live output. Each pulse selects the next channel.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click a component first. HTML: use controls directly.

1. Press Next channel to select 25, 50, 75, then 10 again.
2. The gauge and value display share the selected output; Channel shows the selected input number.
3. Press Reset channel to return to channel 1 and its value of 10.
SMART COMPONENTS  /  07 OF 15
Shift memory · eight stored bits

1. Turn Data on and press Shift. Each pulse advances every cell once.
2. Both registers sample together: the next register receives the previous final cell.
3. Clear memory resets all eight cells. Current value → value is the shared-clock cascade.
value → value
Shared pulse + reset
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click a component first. HTML: use controls directly.

1. Data chooses the bit inserted at the next pulse. Shift advances both registers together.
2. Turn Data on, press Shift once, then turn Data off and keep pressing Shift to move a single bit.
3. After eight shifts in total, the bit reaches Last stored bit. Clear memory empties both registers.

LED patterns · Boolean crossings and row bytes
The left matrix lights row/column intersections. The right matrix uses eight independent byte patterns.
r1
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click a component first. HTML: use controls directly.

1. Use the four toggles to combine odd/even rows and columns on the left matrix.
2. Click the Top row byte number to enter 129 (both ends) or 255 (all eight LEDs).
3. The remaining seven smiley rows stay fixed. Each row uses bit 128 at the left and bit 1 at the right.
SMART COMPONENTS  /  09 OF 15
Count down, reset, repeat
The counter reaches zero, emits completion, and resets itself in settling rounds before the next screen redraw.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click controls. HTML: use them directly. Inputs… shows the actual wiring.

1. Turn Run on. Count cycles 3 → 2 → 1 → 3; zero exists briefly inside the settling sequence.
2. The Completed cycles counter still sees every reached pulse. Stop/Resume preserves the cycle.
3. Pause and Step the simulation to inspect feedback without changing the component wiring.
reached → its own reset

The completion edge reaches every observer,
even though the display may skip zero.
SMART COMPONENTS  /  10 OF 15
Completion stops the clock
The counter’s reached output passes through NOT and disables its own pulse generator.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click controls. HTML: use them directly. Inputs… shows the actual wiring.

1. The countdown starts automatically; at zero, the pulse generator is disabled and stays low.
2. Press Reset to 3 to start a new countdown. A held reached signal does not restart it.
3. Inspect Inputs… on the pulse generator: enable comes from NOT done.
SMART COMPONENTS  /  11 OF 15
Reset the count and remember to stop
A Stop latch retains completion after resetting the counter clears reached.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click controls. HTML: use them directly. Inputs… shows the actual wiring.

1. Press Restart to clear the Stop latch. The countdown resets itself to 3 when it reaches zero.
2. The Stop latch stays set, keeping the clock off even though reached is false again.
3. Press Restart for another cycle. This memory is why reset-and-stop needs a latch.
reached → reset + Stop.set
SMART COMPONENTS  /  12 OF 15
The same memory, built three ways
SR, cross-connected NOR gates, and cross-connected NAND gates retain a bit after Set/Reset is released.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click controls. HTML: use them directly. Inputs… shows the actual wiring.

1. With both controls off, all three memories start X (unknown). Turn Set on, then off: Q stays true.
2. Turn Reset on, then off: Q stays false. The NOT gates make the NAND inputs active-low.
3. Both controls on is a conflict. Releasing both together must not invent a stored bit.
Dedicated memory
Cross-coupled NOR
Cross-coupled NAND
SMART COMPONENTS  /  13 OF 15
One edge, one consistent snapshot
Two flip-flops share a clock. The second stores the first’s previous Q, never its newly sampled value.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click controls. HTML: use them directly. Inputs… shows the actual wiring.

1. Turn Data on. First Clock: A becomes true and B stays false. Second Clock: B becomes true.
2. Change Numeric data, then Clock. The numeric register samples only on the clock’s rising edge.
3. Reset has priority over a simultaneous clock. Held-high clock levels never capture repeatedly.
SMART COMPONENTS  /  14 OF 15
Ring, Johnson, and decoded decade
A shared clock drives a seeded ring, a Johnson feedback register, and a 4017-style decade counter.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click controls. HTML: use them directly. Inputs… shows the actual wiring.

1. Press Clock: the ring circulates one true bit; Johnson feeds back the inverse of its final bit.
2. Ring repeats every 4 clocks, Johnson every 8, and the decoded decade every 10.
3. Reset restores the ring seed and clears Johnson/decade. Inspect Inputs… to see the Johnson feedback.
One-hot seed; reset restores q1
Inverted last stage → first stage
SMART COMPONENTS  /  15 OF 15
A loop with real time between changes
NOT feeds a one-second Delay, whose output feeds NOT. The delay stores each transition and schedules it later.
TRY THIS · Editor: double-click controls. HTML: use them directly. Inputs… shows the actual wiring.

1. The delayed output alternates once per second; the positive delay gives the loop a time boundary.
2. Pause stops active simulation time. Step inspects the next round/event; Resume continues.
3. A zero-delay self-inverting loop cannot settle and should report a visible loop error.
NOT output returns to Delay input
